chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever says "Peace be upon you" (al-Salamu alaykum), it is ten good deeds. And whoever says "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God" (al-Salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah), it is twenty good deeds. And whoever says "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings" (al-Salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh), it is thirty good deeds.'

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ: The Islamic greeting of peace — a religious salutation carrying spiritual merit
key_terms.بَرَكَاتُهُ: His blessings — divine blessings, often paired with mercy in formal greetings
key_terms.حَسَنَات: Good deeds; meritorious acts recorded in one's spiritual account
key_terms.رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ: The mercy of God — a divine attribute frequently invoked in greetings and supplications

ai.seo_question: How many good deeds does saying as-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh earn in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the Islamic greeting carries spiritual merit proportional to its completeness. The basic greeting earns ten good deeds, adding 'wa rahmatullah' doubles this to twenty, and the full greeting with 'wa barakatuh' earns thirty good deeds. This teaching reflects the Islamic emphasis on greeting as an act of worship that cultivates brotherhood and divine reward.
